options.text: Where do you all bunk down?
Point me toward your base? I've got trade in mind.
Where's the nearest camp of yours?
I'd like to visit your people. Which way do I go?
If I ever need walls around me, where are yours?
Give me directions to your post?
Where does your command sit?
Mark my map — where's home for you?
If I follow your cook-smoke, where do I end up?
Which way to your gates?
Do any of your camps take travelers for the night?
Your command post — where do I find it?
Where's your headquarters?
Tell me where your camp is.
Where are your walls weakest?
How many of you are garrisoned near here?
Where do you keep your stores?
Which road leads to your gate?
Show me your positions on a map.
Where can I find your commander?
Where do your soldiers sleep?
Where does your water come from?
Every fort has a back way in. Where's yours?
What do your signal fires mean?
Any settlements near here?
Who holds this stretch of land?
I'm a little lost. Where am I, exactly?
Where could a traveler shelter around here?
Where do people trade in these parts?
What's the biggest landmark around?
Does this road follow the river?
How far to anything with a roof?
Where does your territory end?
Who else is out here besides you?
Where does this road lead?
Are you camped close by?
Where are your enemies dug in?
If I wanted to hurt your rivals, where would I start?
Where should I steer clear of, enemy-wise?
You know where the other side camps?
Mark the enemy's position for me.
What did your scouts find out there?
Where's the enemy stretched thin?
Who's your nearest hostile neighbor, and where?
I'm hunting the same people you are. Where do I look?
I'll trade you news for news. Where's the enemy?
Whose watchfires are those on the horizon?
I have unfinished business with your rivals. Point me at them.
You're an officer. Where do the enemy lines run?
Give me the briefing you'd give your own scouts.
Where will the enemy press next?
Share your campaign map with me.
Where does the real front run these days?
Where's the enemy making trouble for you?
Who are you at war with?
Where's the fighting these days?
Where's the enemy camped?
Which side is winning out here?
I'd pay good coin for enemy positions.
Where did the last battle happen?
Any enemy maps you've captured?
Taken any prisoners who talked?
Do you have spies in the other camps?
When's your next raid, and where?
What's the latest from the front?
Point me at your enemies and I'll thin them out for you.
When do your patrols change over?
How often do your rounds pass this way?
When's the next patrol due through here?
How long is a watch shift for you?
Do your patrols keep walking after dark?
What route do your patrols run?
Is there ever a gap between patrols?
Which roads do you watch closest?
When does your relief arrive?
How far out do your patrols range?
When's the safest hour to travel your roads?
If I hear your horn, what does it mean?
What's your patrol schedule?
Who's on watch tonight?
Where are your blind spots?
When does the watch rotate?
How many walk each patrol?
Which paths do your patrols skip?
How many sentries stand your wall?
How fast can you raise an alarm?
Do you even watch the roads after midnight?
Your patrols look thin lately. Short-handed?
Whose road is this?
Who watches this road?
Will I be stopped again if I keep walking this road?
Anyone charging tolls out here?
Any bandits working this stretch?
Any checkpoints ahead?
Much traffic come through here?
When was the last trouble on this road?
Does anyone use this road at night?
Do traders' carts still run this way?
What's over that ridge?
What's in the forest beyond here?
I saw ruins to the east. Know anything about them?
Any caves worth knowing about nearby?
What's down in the valley?
I saw smoke over the hills. Yours?
Where's good water around here?
What's the highest ground around?
Is there a way around the swamp?
Is the mountain pass open?
How far to the coast from here?
Anything out here that bites worse than soldiers?
What's the safest way east?
Which routes should I avoid?
Is it safe to travel after dark?
Any shortcuts through this territory?
Where's the best river crossing?
Which way do the caravans go?
Which road gets me through with the fewest questions?
I'm hauling goods. Which road won't get them taken?
Best way west without trouble?
Which paths stay quiet these days?
What should I avoid out here at night?
What comes out after dark in these parts?
Whose fires are those out in the dark?
Is it madness to keep walking tonight?
What was that sound just now?
What should I call out so your sentries don't jump me in the dark?
Where's the nearest safe fire tonight?
Do raids come with the full moon out here?
Which roads go bad after sundown?
How long until first light?
I know we've traded blows. I still need directions.
Business is business. Where's the nearest market road?
You'd rather I wander your lands blind? Tell me what's ahead.
Humor me — where's your base?
Truce for a minute. What's down this road?
Forget what happened between us. Who patrols this stretch?
My coin spends the same as anyone's. What's out east?
Your patrols keep missing me. Where will the next one be?
What brings your patrol this far out?
Seen anyone else on this road today?
I crossed fresh tracks back there. Yours?
Are you lot lost, or am I?
Where will you camp tonight?
How far does your ground run out here?
Anything I should know about the trail ahead?
Is there water enough out here for two more days' walking?
Mind if I walk with your patrol a stretch?
You're a long way from home.
Where do your supplies come in from?
What are you short of these days?
When does the next supply run arrive?
Can I buy off your surplus?
If I brought goods to sell, which road should I use?
What's grain fetching out here?
How deep are your stores running?
Which routes need guarding? I might take the work.

negative: Our walls are for us. You get the wire.
You want the line's address? Earn it or dig for it.
neutral: There's a camp. It has a direction. That's all you get today.
The line sits where the digging is. You'll know it by the mud.
positive: Follow the trench-smoke north till your boots sink. Knock loud, walk slow.
Home is where the shovels are. Head that way — tell them the line sent you.
You've earned the walk. Warm food, cold bunks, honest mud. Go on.

negative: Base locations are restricted. Move along.
That information is above your clearance. It will stay there.
neutral: Installations are need-to-know. You don't need to know.
Follow the marked road and you'll be met before you're lost.
positive: Cleared for release. Bearing's on your map — announce yourself at the outer marker.
Forward operating site is a short march out. Gate staff will have your name.
Take the maintained road. If a sentry stops you, say you're logged as friendly.

negative: Our tents move. Your questions do not catch them.
Ask the dunes. They keep our address better than I do.
neutral: Where do the swallows sleep? Somewhere out of the wind. So do we.
The camp finds its guests. Guests do not find the camp.
positive: Walk toward the evening star until you smell cardamom. The fires will rise to meet you.
The path is under the third ridge, where the shadow pools at dusk. You are expected.
Follow the camel tracks that vanish. Where they end, we begin.

negative: Ha. Write your question down, roll it tight, eat it.
You ask where we sleep? Closer than you'd like, friend.
The only map you get is the road out. It's behind you.
neutral: Curious one, aren't you. Curiosity fills trenches.
That's line business. Yours is walking.
positive: Even for you, some doors stay shut. Nothing personal — everything's personal, actually.
Ask me about the weather instead. The weather won't get us shelled.

negative: Denied. And the request itself is now in your file.
That question is a threat indicator. Ask another.
You are fishing in a restricted pond, civilian.
neutral: Negative. Operational security is not a courtesy I can waive.
Request denied. Standard procedure, nothing personal.
positive: Even friendlies don't get that one. Doctrine before friendship.
Can't release it. What I can do is walk you somewhere safer to stand.

negative: You ask the mirage for its house. Enjoy the search.
A knife asks the sheath where it lives. The sheath smiles.
Dig anywhere. You will find sand, and sand, and then us — too late.
neutral: The desert has many rooms and lends none of them.
Some questions are doors. That one is a wall.
positive: Friend, do not carry that answer. It is heavy, and men die of the weight.
Even the tea does not know where the kettle sleeps.

negative: There's mud in every direction. Pick one.
Somewhere out there. Walk until someone shouts.
neutral: There's a road east. It goes east. That's its whole trick.
Settlements come and go out here. Mostly go.
Follow the ruts. Carts are smarter than people about where to walk.
positive: Keep the sunrise on your left shoulder and you'll hit the trade track by noon.
There's a hamlet past the burned mill. They'll sell you bread if you don't mention us.

negative: Consult a map. Not mine.
Navigation assistance is not on offer today.
neutral: General bearings only: settlement traffic runs the east road. Beyond that, ask there.
You're inside our operating area. Edges are a day's walk in most directions.
The river road is maintained. The rest I wouldn't certify.
positive: Marked route east, two klicks, then follow the cairns. You'll raise a village by dusk.
Stay on the graded road and you'll pass two of our markers before any trouble.

negative: Every direction is far, walker. Start early.
The land belongs to whoever the land is currently eating.
neutral: Roads here are like promises. Some are kept.
There is a well two ridges over. Where there is water, there are people. Sometimes kind ones.
Walk with the wind at your back and you will arrive somewhere. The desert decides where.
positive: Past the white rocks there is a market that asks no names. Mention the shade and pay less.
Follow the old riverbed. Dead rivers still know the way to towns.

negative: Give you our enemy's door? You haven't even earned ours.
No. You'd sell it to them by supper.
neutral: That arithmetic isn't for strangers.
The enemy is that way. The details cost more than you've paid.
positive: Lean in. Their camp squats past the ridge — hit it at dawn and count for us.
We've bled for this map. You've bled with us, so look: there. Bring back their banner.
Their walls are where our shells land. Follow the thunder, friend.

negative: Hostile positions are classified. Especially from you.
You don't have the clearance, and frankly you don't have the trust.
neutral: Target data is restricted. Assistance in earning access is available.
Negative. That release requires a standing relationship you don't have yet.
positive: Releasing hostile grid to a verified friendly. Copy it once, burn nothing, tell no one.
Enemy encampment plotted at the marked bearing. If you act on it, we never spoke.
You've earned target access. Coordinates follow. Advise you strike with the sun behind you.

negative: You hunt with wolves you have not fed. No.
Our enemies' names are not coins for your purse.
neutral: The scorpion does not point out the other scorpion. Professional courtesy.
Patience. Trust ripens slower than dates.
positive: Their fires burn beyond the salt flat. Go in the cold hours; their sentries dream of home.
The vipers nest where the two hills kiss. Strike while the shadow is longest, friend.
We have watched them a season. Now you may borrow our eyes. There — where the crows circle.

negative: An officer's map is paid for in casualties. Yours isn't the currency.
I brief my line, not strangers with opinions.
neutral: Briefings are for people who dig when told. You don't dig.
I've buried men for guessing at this. I won't hand it to you free.
positive: Fine. Officer to irregular: their strength sits past the ford. Numbers favor us. They always do, eventually.
Here's the picture I give my sergeants: enemy there, us here, mud everywhere. Memorize it.
You've carried weight for the line, so carry this: their forward camp, one valley over.

negative: You're asking a commissioned officer to commit a breach. Bold. Denied.
My scouts earn their briefings. You've earned an escort out.
neutral: That briefing has a distribution list. You're not on it.
I don't freelance intelligence, civilian. Chain of command exists for a reason.
positive: Command assessment, verbal only: hostile axis runs the low ground. Their camp anchors it. Marked.
I'll authorize a one-time release. Enemy laager at the plotted point. Use it before it goes stale.
Consider yourself a deputized asset. The opposing force masses beyond the tree line — there.

negative: The falcon does not report to the field mouse.
I lead by knowing what others do not. I will keep leading.
neutral: A captain's knowledge is his tent pole. Pull it and everything falls.
Ask me for water, for bread, for shade. Not for this.
positive: Come, look at the sand table. This wadi — their camp. This hour — their weakness. Go quietly.
I will tell you what my riders know: the enemy sleeps fat behind the gap in the hills.
You have kept faith with the shade, so the shade opens its hand: their position, there.

negative: Our wars are our own. Yours is finding the road out.
You ask about our enemies like you aren't one. Funny.
The front doesn't send news. It sends stretchers.
neutral: There's a war. It's around. Specifics are for people in it.
Who's winning? The flies. The flies are always winning.
You want battle news, enlist. We issue shovels same day.
positive: Careful, friend. Names of enemies are heavier than they look.
Not yet. Ask me again when your boots have more of our mud on them.

negative: Hostile force data is classified, and you're closer to hostile than force.
Your interest in our enemies is noted. And filed.
No comment, and the asking cost you nothing only this once.
neutral: Ongoing operations are not discussed with unaffiliated persons.
There is a conflict. Its particulars are managed. That's your briefing.
I can neither confirm nor locate anything for you today.
positive: Soon, maybe. Trust accrues like interest, and yours is still maturing.
That's one clearance level above where we stand, friend. Keep standing with us.

negative: You ask who we fight. Today, perhaps whoever asks too much.
Our quarrels are old and private, like family debts.
The desert eats armies. Which one is not your concern.
neutral: Wars here are like wind. Always somewhere, never where you point.
Who is winning? The sand. The sand is undefeated.
When the tea has been shared more times, perhaps the names will pour too.
positive: Patience, friend of the shade. Fruit picked green sours the whole basket.
Walk with us a while longer. Then we will speak of vipers and where they nest.

negative: The patrol comes when it comes. Usually right behind you.
Our rounds are our business. Being found by them is yours.
neutral: Rounds pass often enough. Often enough for what? Exactly.
Shifts change when the relief stops complaining and starts walking.
The line walks its wire at all hours. Sleep is a rumor.
positive: Next sweep loops the east track before dusk. Wave early, wave big.
Relief column moves at first light. Travel behind it and you'll have quiet roads.
We double the wire watch after bad nights. Last night was bad. Walk loud today.

negative: Patrol timings are classified. Persisting will classify you.
That's operational tempo. Not yours to know.
neutral: Rotations occur on schedule. The schedule is the part you don't get.
Coverage is continuous. Treat every road as watched and you'll be accurate enough.
Patrols are frequent by design. Design is classified.
positive: Between you and the gatepost: south leg turns over at dusk. Cross before, not after.
Next foot patrol sweeps the ridge road within the hour. Friendly faces, if yours stays friendly.
Our long-range element is out two days. Roads west are thinner than usual. Plan accordingly.

negative: We pass when the shadow passes. Try to time a shadow.
Ask the moon when we walk. She keeps our diary.
neutral: The watch changes as the wind changes. You will feel it, not see it.
We are behind you more often than ahead of you. Let that schedule your day.
Patrols? We prefer to say the desert strolls, and sometimes we stroll with it.
positive: The riders swing wide of the salt pan until the heat breaks. Travel it at midday, friend.
Our walkers rest at the old cistern near sundown. Pass there and you pass among friends.
Tonight the watch is thick to the north. Keep south of the ridge and the road is yours.

negative: Asking about our watch is how people end up counted by it.
Blind spots? We're standing in one. Just you and me. Think about that.
Short-handed, sure. Never too short to handle you.
neutral: That question has barbed wire around it.
Watch business stays inside the watch.
positive: Even friends don't get the roster. The roster is how we stay alive.
Ha — you sound like an inspector. Inspectors get shown the nice trench only.

negative: That is exactly the question an infiltrator asks. Noted, timestamped, remembered.
Sentry counts are classified. Your interest in them is now also on file.
Keep probing our watch and the watch will probe back.
neutral: Security posture isn't shared. Standing order, no exceptions.
Negative on all of that. The perimeter answers to no questionnaire.
positive: Friend or not, the watch bill stays sealed. It protects you too, believe it.
If our coverage worried me, I'd fix it, not discuss it. It doesn't worry me.

negative: You count our sentries? Count the stars instead. Same use, longer life.
The night has holes only for those we allow to fall through them.
Ask again about our watch and you will meet it personally.
neutral: The tent does not show its stitching to the wind.
We watch what needs watching. Currently, that includes you.
positive: Even to a friend, the pattern of the watch is a bride's face. Veiled.
Why count our eyes, friend? Enough are open. Always enough.

negative: This road belongs to whoever holds it. Today: us. Keep moving.
Watched enough to catch you. That's the number that matters.
neutral: It's the line's road. We sweep it when the mud allows.
Bandits tried this stretch once. The ditch remembers them.
Carts pass on quota days. Otherwise it's boots and crows.
positive: Our section walks it twice a day, more when the guns get chatty. You're covered till the fork.
Road's ours and it's quiet. The tolls died with the last toll-takers.
Stay on it till the burned oak, then you're past our wire and into luck.

negative: This is a controlled route. You're the current control problem.
Who watches it? You're talking to him. Move along.
neutral: Route is under regular observation. Conduct yourself accordingly.
Checkpoint ahead at the bridge. Have your business ready to state.
Bandit activity is suppressed on this corridor. We keep it that way.
positive: Corridor's green through the crossroads. Past that, our coverage thins — stay alert.
You'll hit one checkpoint at the mill. Give them your name; it's in the friendly log.
We run this road on a tight loop. Trouble finds you, hold position — response is fast.

negative: The road is watched. Mostly, right now, you are the thing watched.
Whose road? The road of whoever wakes up still holding it.
neutral: Many eyes rest on this road. Not all of them blink.
Tolls, no. Debts, sometimes. The road keeps its own ledger.
Night traffic exists. It prefers not to be discussed.
positive: The road is under our shade to the twin palms. Beyond that, walk like a stranger again.
Trouble avoids this stretch, friend. Trouble knows who it belongs to.
Carts pass on market days under our eye. Join one; company shortens miles.

negative: Over the ridge? More war. Under it too, if you dig.
Terrain questions from you make my trigger finger philosophical.
neutral: Ridge hides a dead village. Everything useful was carried off, including the roofs.
The valley floods, the forest hides deserters, the caves eat lanterns. Charming country.
Good water at the shattered well, if you boil it and your standards are low.
positive: Past the ridge is a meadow the shells missed. Prettiest thing for miles. Enjoy it for us.
The caves north are dry and deep. We stashed matches there once. Might still be some.
That smoke is ours — cook fires, not signal fires. Somebody finally shot a boar.

negative: Terrain data supports operations. You're not an operation. Yet.
Ask the ridge yourself. Take your time up there in the open.
neutral: High ground east is surveyed. Low ground floods seasonal. Plan around both.
The ruins predate all three banners. Structurally unsound, occasionally occupied.
The pass is open but unimproved. Rockfall risk after rain.
positive: Over the ridge: open farmland, one abandoned watchtower, decent sightlines. Safe in daylight.
Reliable water at the spring by the split boulder. We test it monthly. It passes.
Coast is three days on the river road. Two if you don't stop to admire our engineering.

negative: Beyond the ridge is more of what is behind you. Disappointment.
The land answers politely to polite guests. You are neither, yet.
neutral: The valley holds an old orchard gone wild. The fruit is bitter and the shade is sweet.
Those ruins were a proud town once. Pride is poor mortar.
The swamp can be skirted on the deer paths. Deer are honest guides.
positive: Beyond the ridge a spring hides under the fig roots. Drink deep and thank the tree, friend.
The caves keep cool even at noon. We have slept there; the sand inside tells no tales.
That smoke is a wedding, not a war. This week, at least, the hills celebrate.

negative: Safest way is away. All roads qualify.
Routes are safe until they aren't. You'll find the boundary fast.
neutral: East road is dull, which is the best thing a road can be.
Avoid the ford after rain and the tavern after payday.
Caravans hug the ridgeline. Slower, but caravans still exist, so.
positive: Take the sunken lane, friend. Ugly walking, but nobody ambushes a ditch they can't see into.
Go west by the quarry track. Our guns overlook it the whole way. Best escort money can't buy.
Cross the river at the cattle ford, not the bridge. Bridges collect the wrong crowd.

negative: Route planning services are for cleared personnel. Walk where you like. Carefully.
The safest route for you is out of my sector. Any bearing.
neutral: Main east road is patrolled and posted. Secondary tracks are travel-at-own-risk.
After dark, movement is discouraged. That's guidance, not a threat.
The river crossing at the mill is inspected and stable. Use that one.
positive: Recommended routing: east road to the crossroads, then the marked trail. Both under watch.
Hauling cargo? Take the convoy road on supply days. Nobody touches what moves with us.
West passage is clean this week. Our patrols just swept it end to end.

negative: Every road is safe until the sand shifts. The sand is shifting.
Ask me tomorrow. Tonight, no road would forgive you.
neutral: Travel with the cool hours and the busy birds. Both avoid trouble professionally.
The shortcut exists. It is shorter in distance and longer in regret.
Cross the river where the women wash clothes. Danger avoids witnesses.
positive: Walk the shepherd trail at dawn, friend. It is watched by kind eyes the whole way.
The quiet paths run behind the dunes. Quiet because we keep them so. They are yours today.
Go with the salt caravan when it passes. Its guides owe us shade and will owe you courtesy.

negative: At night, avoid us. There. Free advice.
The dark hides wolves, deserters, and worse: sentries who startle.
neutral: Avoid lights that move and silences that don't.
Night belongs to whoever's most tired of living. Don't compete.
That sound? Wire on wind. Probably. The line finds out at dawn.
positive: Stay near our wire tonight, friend. Shout 'shovels' at the sentry and he'll wave you close.
Our fire's the low red one by the berm. Cold night's shorter with company.
Dawn's maybe four hours off. Sit with the reserve squad; they brew something almost like tea.

negative: After dark, unidentified movement gets one challenge. Sometimes.
Night protocol is strict. You're one silhouette away from learning it.
neutral: Avoid the perimeter approaches at night. Sentries challenge once, per doctrine.
Unlit roads are uncontrolled roads. Govern yourself accordingly.
That sound was an animal or a problem. We're paid to assume the problem.
positive: Call out 'traveler, friendly' at any post and hold still. You're in the log; you'll be fine.
Safest fire tonight is our forward picket. Announce early — night watch likes warnings.
First light in five hours. Shelter at the signal tower; the crew expects stragglers.

negative: The night here has our manners. Do not test its patience.
What comes out after dark? We do. You have your answer and your warning.
neutral: Avoid still water and still men. Both drown travelers.
The fires you see are stories. Some welcome guests. Some collect them.
Walk loud if you must walk. The night mistakes quiet men for prey — or rivals.
positive: Sleep near the tamarisk, friend. Our night walkers pass it twice and will pass over you kindly.
The moon is with you tonight. Keep her on your right and you keep our blessing.
Come to the low fire with the copper kettle. Night tea is bitter and the company gentle.

vengeful: Directions? To your grave, gladly. It's nearby and we dug it personally.
Eleven names, and you want a map. The nerve is almost admirable. Almost.
negative: You spilled our blood and want directions. The road out. Fast.
The only thing I'll point at you is already pointed.
neutral: You've cost us, and you know it. Ask small questions and walk smaller.
Truce, he says. The dead don't sign truces. But fine — the road's clear to the fork. Go.
positive: You settled some of what you owed, so: east track's safe. We're square until you make us not.
The line remembers your sins and your service both. Today the service wins. Barely. Head south.

vengeful: You have confirmed kills on this command and questions in your mouth. Astonishing. Leave.
Weapons-free is one order away. Your directions are: anywhere else.
negative: You're red-flagged with casualties attached. No information will be released.
Your record includes our dead. This conversation is over-generous already.
neutral: Given your history, cooperation is limited: road's open east. That's all you get.
You've cost this command personnel. I'll answer nothing that helps you cost us more.
positive: Your ledger with us is complicated. Balance says: market road's two klicks south. Don't reset it.
Restitution is noted, casualties are not forgotten. Travel east. Stay visible while you do.

vengeful: You come to the well you filled with blood, asking to drink. Poetic. Fatal, but poetic.
The sand under your feet holds our brothers. It is listening for your last step.
negative: Directions, from us, for you? The vulture gives better ones. Follow him.
Your hands are red and your tongue is bold. One of these will shorten your road.
neutral: We remember what you took. Still — the road east is open. Even debts respect the road.
Bold, to ask. The market track runs past the dry well. Walk it owing us, and walk quickly.
positive: Blood dries, friend, when enough kindness rains on it. East, past the cairns. Go in peace, this once.
The scales between us tremble. I will steady them: safe road south. Do not touch the scales again.

negative: Far from our walls, close to our patience's end. State your business.
Out here there's no wire between us. Remember that.
neutral: We walk where the line needs eyes. Today it needs them here.
Seen nobody but crows and you. The crows were better company.
Tracks are ours. If they weren't, we'd be running, not talking.
positive: Long way from home, sure. Home is where the shovel lands. Tonight, that hollow there.
Trail ahead is clear to the second ridge. After that, keep your head on a swivel, friend.
Walk with us to the stream if you like. The pace is miserable and the jokes are worse.

negative: This patrol is tasked. You're an unplanned contact. Don't become an unplanned incident.
Distance from base means nothing. Reach is doctrine.
neutral: Routine reconnaissance. That's the whole answer you're cleared for.
Negative contacts today besides yourself. Keep it a quiet log.
Trail ahead is unassessed past the creek. Treat it as such.
positive: We're sweeping the far arc — long walk, good boots. Road behind us is clean, use it.
You can move with the patrol to the waypoint. Stay in file, don't wander off the track.
Fresh water's cached at the leaning pine. Take a fair share and leave the cache covered.

negative: Far from walls, yes. We never had walls. You are far from yours.
The patrol you see is the smallest part of the patrol you don't.
neutral: We go where the sand goes. It has been going here lately.
The only tracks that matter are the ones you did not notice.
The trail ahead is honest until the black rocks. After that, it starts telling stories.
positive: Walk with us to the well, friend. The desert is smaller with company and larger with none.
We camp where the wind forgets to look. Tonight, that gully. There is room by the fire.
Ahead the trail is swept and safe. We swept it. Consider it our gift to your boots.

negative: Stores are counted, crates are counted, you are counted. Move along.
Supply questions from strangers end up in the wrong ledgers.
neutral: Supplies come from sacrifice and a road I won't name. Mostly sacrifice.
We're short of everything except mud and resolve. Standing order.
Grain fetches whatever hungry men pay. So: everything.
positive: Between us — the column comes up the north road on quota days. Sell to me before it arrives, prices are kinder.
Short on salt, nails, and reasons to smile. Bring any of the three and we'll talk numbers.
There's escort work on the ration road if your arm's strong and your questions are few.

negative: Logistics data is more classified than the war itself. File your curiosity elsewhere.
Asking a quartermaster about supply lines is asking to be inventoried. Don't.
neutral: Procurement is centralized, distribution is scheduled, and neither is your business.
Shortages exist. Their specifics are managed above your involvement.
Market rates are posted at the trade point. Consult the board, not me.
positive: Resupply convoy runs the graded road twice weekly. Vendors get right of way if they're on the ledger — you are.
Current shortfalls: binding wire, lamp oil, dried fruit. Deliver any and invoice me directly.
Route security contracts are open. Standard rates, paid on delivery confirmation. Interested?

negative: Where does our water come from? The sky. Complain to it.
You count our sacks and I will count your steps. Neither ends well.
neutral: Supplies arrive the way dew arrives. Quietly, and gone by the time you ask.
What are we short of? Rain. Always rain. The rest we manage.
Prices here follow the wind. Today the wind is moderate.
positive: The caravans slip in by the old salt path, friend. Meet them at the cistern and trade under our shade.
Bring dates, rope, or good cloth and the camp will open its purse to you gladly.
We pay well for quiet guards on the water road. Quieter the guard, heavier the purse.
